meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/06, Monday 10 June 2024). Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: June 2024 series, despite the download folder's Nov 24 label. Coded in the same sitting as OCR-JUN24-F-P3. Interleaved crossover: J560/03 q19, q20, q21, q22 and q23 reappear here as q2, q3, q4, q5 and q6, with marks matching item for item (2, 3, 7, 9, 4 — 25 of the 100). No per-question total is printed, so the whole-paper sum against the published 100 is the only check, and this file passes it.

coding_notes: q2, q3, q4, q5 and q6 are J560/03 q19, q20, q21, q22 and q23 and carry identical skill tags, kinds and mark splits to that file, by design.
mark_split is derived from OCR's part totals and partial-credit routes rather than quoted; see OCR-JUN24-F-P1 for the reasoning.

q1 (match three described relationships to six sketched graphs) tagged sketching_functions alone, following the OCR-JUN25-F-P1 q15 ruling. The three relationships are a linear conversion, an inverse proportion and a direct proportion, so direct_proportion and inverse_proportion could each be added; the demand is recognising standard shapes, and sketching_functions credits fewer skills.
q8a and q8b are a CUBIC, not a quadratic — tagged sketching_functions (with substitution for the table), since quadratic_functions would be a false claim.

q10a tagged simple_arithmetic and q10b algebraic_proof: (a) is a one-mark numerical demonstration on a specific set of eight numbers and (b) is the general proof. Tagging (a) as algebraic_proof would credit a proof the student has not done.
q11a tagged relative_frequency then frequency_trees — the phrase 'relative frequency' is the question's own, and the counts come off the tree.
q18 tagged sine_rule then cosine_rule: the mark scheme's route is a sine rule in the first triangle for the shared side, then a cosine rule in the second.
